en: Vādhūla Gṛhya Sūtra 2. Darśapūrṇamāsa (Puroḍāśī).
N rechecked 96, ñan 18; K rechecked 97, February 9; K rechecked 98, May 24; N rechecked 97, February 19; M rechecked 97, February 24. K to be checked from 2.4.4.11 (24a1).
The New and Full Moon Sacrifices (Puroḍāśa-offerings).

2.1.1.1. Having offered a sacrificial fuel-stick (*idhma*) consisting of twenty-one pieces of wood with well-cleaned chips, under the formula "Today is the fast-day," he places [the fire] upon the *āhavanīya* for the *agnihotra*. He places one piece of wood on the *gārhapatya*, one on the *anvāhāryapacana*, and one on the *āhavanīya*; thereafter, he may place as many more as he desires. 2.1.1.2. On the fast-day of the new moon (*amāvāsyā*), having curdled the remains of the *agnihotra* milk, he sets it aside for the purpose of curdling the sacrificial oblation (*havirātañcana*). 2.1.1.3. Having gone out further, he cuts a branch of the *palāśa* tree which is directed either eastward or northward and has not dried tips, with the formula: "For food, thee! (*iṣe tvā*).
2.1.1.4. With the formula, "For strength, thee" (TS 1.1.1.a2), he strokes her.

2.1.1.5. Having gone with her, he drives away the calves: with "Ye are winds" (TS 1.1.1.b) for the males, and with "Ye are helpers" (TS 1.1.1.b) for the females. 2.1.1.6. He consecrates the cows with the formula, "May the divine Savitṛ impel you for the most excellent rite; swell, O inviolable ones, as a portion rich in strength for Indra and the gods; may he separate you [from the calves]" (TS 1.1.1.c–f).
2.1.1.7. With the words, “May you be many and firm with this lord of cattle” (TS 1.1.1.g), he consecrates either the sacrificer, or a bull, or the cow-pen.

2.1.1.8. With the words, “Protect the cattle of the sacrificer” (TS 1.1.1.h), he hides a branch of the *palāśa* tree in the northern part of the fire-hall, or at the post of the *agniṣṭha* cart. 2.1.1.9. Having placed the seat to the west of the *gārhapatya* fire with the words, “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ” (TS 1.2.1.a), he takes it up with the words, “I take thee with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan; thou art the proclaimer of the sacrifice” (TS 1.2.1.b).
2.1.1.10. With the words, "The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away," he heats [the grass] over the Gārhapatya fire.
2.1.1.11. With the words, "Go along the wide mid-region," he goes halfway toward the sacrificial grass, between the altar and the rubbish-heap (utkara).
2.1.1.12. With the words, "This prayer has gone forth to the gods; may the sacrificial grass sit here, pleasing to the gods," he looks down at the altar.

2.1.1.13. With the formula, “Thou art chosen around by the gods,” he points out that place where the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is to be cut; with the formula, “Thou art grown by rain” (TS 1.1.2d–e), [he points it out]. 2.1.1.14. With the formula, “For the gods, thee, for those whose sacrificial grass is upright,” he strokes upward a tuft of grass.
2.1.1.15. With the formula, “O divine sacrificial grass, do not follow me, nor go across me” (TS 1.1.2f), he approaches [the grass].

2.1.1.16. With the formula, “May I succeed in thy joint,” (TS 1.1.2.g), he places [the blade] down with the knife. 2.1.1.17. With the formula, “May I, thy cutter, not be harmed,” (TS 1.1.2.h), he cuts. 2.1.1.18.

Having balanced the knife in his left hand, he touches the cuttings with the formula, “O divine sacrificial grass, possessing a hundred blades, grow forth! (TS 1.1.2.i, var.), and he touches himself with the formula, “Possessing a thousand blades, may we grow forth! (TS 1.1.2.i, var.).
2.1.1.19. Having touched water, he places the first handful with the formula, "Protect from contact with the earth" (TS 1.1.2.k). He announces it to the *prastara* [bundle of grass]. 2.1.1.20.
He cuts an odd number of handfuls—seven, nine, eleven, or thirteen—as he considers appropriate.
2.1.1.21. Then, with the formula, "Thou art the girdle for Aditi" (TS 1.1.2.m1), he three times winds the binding-cloth around the [fire-pan] from left to right.
2.1.1.22. Having spread it out with its ends pointing northward, he places the materials into it with the formula, "I gather thee, well-gathered" (TS 1.1.2.l).
2.1.1.23. With the formula, "Thou art the binding-cloth for Indrāṇī" (TS 1.1.2.m2), he draws it up completely.
2.1.1.24. With the words, “May Pūṣan tie your knot,” he twists [the cord] around crosswise. 2.1.1.25. With the words, “May it not harm you,” he wraps it around in the natural direction.
2.1.1.26. With the words, “I lift you up with the arms of Indra,” he lifts it up.
2.1.1.27. With the formula, "I take [thee] from the head of Bṛhaspati" (TS 1.1.2.2), they place it upon the head.

2.1.1.28. With the formula, "Follow the wide atmosphere" (TS 1.1.2.2), having carried it between the altar and the rubbish-heap (utkara), he deposits it to the north of the Āhavanīya fire with the formula, "Thou art going to the gods" (TS 1.1.2.2). He places it where he considers it secure, not on the ground.
2.2.1.1. He prepares a threefold branch-strainer, he prepares the *veda*, he prepares the altar (*vedi*), and he prepares two stirring-sticks (*mekṣaṇa*).
2.2.1.2. With one of these two, he offers to the ancestors under a tree where the sun shines. 2.2.1.3. He sets aside the other [stirring-stick]; they bring a water-pot.
2.2.1.4. One by one, he places the mortar and pestle, the winnowing basket, the wooden sword, and the pot to the south of the Anvāhāryapacana fire.
2.2.1.5. Having mentally measured out half a vessel of rice, they thresh it to the south of the Anvāhāryapacana fire so as not to spill anything.
2.2.1.6. Having husked them once, he places a pot that is slightly less than full on the fire and pours [the rice] into it.

2.2.1.7. He cooks [the rice] turning toward the south; he does not set it down before the ghee has been poured into it. 2.2.1.8. When he pours the ghee into it, then he sets it down. 2.2.1.9. With the words, “Those who are the counterparts of the ancestors,” he digs up the ground to the south of the Anvāhāryapacana fire with the wooden sword (*sphya*), saying, “The Asuras, those who carry off the fortresses—those who sit near this sacrifice, may Agni drive them away from this sacrifice” (cf. BŚS 2.9:47.6).
2.2.1.10. Having taken a firebrand, he heats [the water] while facing east.

2.2.1.11. With the verse, “May those below rise up, and those above,” he sprinkles [the ground] with the water-pot, saying: “May the middle Fathers, who are gentle, who have gone to the life-breath, who are non-violent and knowers of the *ṛta*—may they protect us, O Fathers, at our invocations” (*TS* 2.6.12.1, var.; cf. *BŚS* 2.8.46.13ff.).

2.2.1.12. Having placed the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*yajñopavīta*), he offers three oblations with the stirring-spoon (*mekṣaṇa*), saying: "To Soma accompanied by the ancestors, *svadhā*! Homage! To Yama accompanied by the Aṅgirases and the ancestors, *svadhā*! Homage! To Agni, the carrier of the offerings to the ancestors (*kavyavāhana*), *svadhā*! Homage! (cf. BŚS 3.10:80.4). 2.2.1.13. He silently throws the stirring-spoon into the fire. 2.2.1.14. Having placed the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*), he purifies himself with a handful of grass.

2.2.1.15. To the west of that [fire], having strewn southward-pointed grass around the Anvāhāryapacana fire, he pours out three water-pots with the formula: “Om! May the fathers cleanse themselves!”—“Om! May the grandfathers cleanse themselves! May the great-grandfathers cleanse themselves! (cf. BŚS 3.10:80.8; 80.19).

2.2.1.16. With the words, “This for you, father,” he offers three wooden ladles (darvī), [reciting]: “Those whom you follow and those who follow you, those who are around you and those with whom you dwell together in the *svadhā*—this is your *svadhā*-abode. With the words, “This for you, grandfather,” [he says]: “Those whom you follow and those who follow you, those who are around you and those with whom you dwell together in the *svadhā*—this is your *svadhā*-abode. With the words, “This for you, great-grandfather,” [he says]: “Those whom you follow and those who follow you, those who are around you and those with whom you dwell together in the *svadhā*...”
"Accompanied by *svadhā*, O you who dwell on *svadhā*! (TS 1.8.5b.1 with variants;
cf. 3.2.5q). "This for you, O grandfathers and great-grandfathers," he says; thus indeed one whose father is still living should offer [the portion].
Having said, "O fathers, rejoice here according to your respective shares" (TS 1.8.5b.2), he turns toward the north and remains seated until the water has subsided.
2.2.1.19. With the words, “*Susandṛśaṃ tvā vayam*,” he gazes toward the Āhavanīya fire, [reciting] “*Maghavan mandiṣīmahi*” (TS 1.8.5c, with variation).

2.2.1.20. With the verse, “*Pra nūnaṃ pūrṇabandhura*,” he worships that very [fire], reciting: “*Stuto yāsi vaśām anu; yojā nv indra te harī*” (TS 1.8.5c2). 2.2.1.21. With the verse, “*Akṣann amīmadanta hi*,” he worships the Gārhapatya fire, reciting: “*Ava priyā te harī*” (TS 1.8.5d).

2.2.1.22. He steps upon the Anvāhāryapacana fire with the verse: “O bulls, mount that chariot...”, [and] with: “O Indra, he who knows the vessel that wins cattle, which is the harnessing of the bay horses, full—yoke the two bay horses that are let loose” (cf. ṚV 1.82. var.). 2.2.1.23. He turns around with the verse: “The Soma-loving fathers have rejoiced... (RV 10.15.14). 2.2.1.24. He smells three times what remains in the cooking pot with the formula: “Those kinsmen who are of one mind, a hundred of them... (cf. BŚS 3.11:80.16f.).

2.2.1.25. He worships with prostrations, saying: “Homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of sap” (TS 3.2.5.s–u); and “Homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of vigor; may I become most excellent” (cf. BŚS 3.11:81.3). 2.2.1.26. With the words, “May the fathers purify themselves,” he pours out three water-vessels, saying: “May the grandfathers purify themselves; may the great-grandfathers purify themselves” (cf.
BŚS 3.10:80.8; 80.19). 2.2.1.27. He cuts off the fringe [of the garment], saying: “This is your garment, O fathers; give me a hero” (cf. BŚS 3.11:80.1).
2.2.1.28. Regarding the Brāhmaṇa passage, “In the latter part of his life, he should have his hair cut” (TB 1.3.10.7), he cuts only the fringe of his garment.

2.2.1.29. He pays homage with the verse, “The fathers have eaten” (TS 1.8.5e): “The fathers have rejoiced; the fathers have been satisfied; the fathers have cleansed themselves. 2.2.1.30. He completes the rite with the verse, “Depart, O Soma-loving fathers” (TS 1.8.5f): “They rejoice in the company [of the gods] on their deep paths.”

2.2.1.31. With the three verses beginning, “O Mind, we now invoke thee” (TS 1.8.5g–i), he invokes the mind, [concluding] with the words, “and may we be united with the Fathers through the Nārāśaṃsa hymn.

2.2.1.32. With the verse, “Whatever [sin we have committed] against the atmosphere, the earth, or the sky” (TS 1.8.5k), he worships the Gārhapatya fire from that very spot, [continuing] with the words, “whatever [we have harmed] our mother or father, O powerful one—may we be sinless.

2.2.1.33. Having placed the sacrificial cord over his left shoulder (yajñopavīta), he goes toward the Āhavanīya fire with the verse, “O Prajāpati, none other than you [possesses] these things” (TS 1.8.14, etc.), [concluding] with the words, “[you are] the lords of all beings and of riches.”
2.2.1.34. Having returned, he pours these ladles together into a vessel, pours water from the water-jar over them, and throws the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) after [the oblations].
2.2.1.35. The Pitṛyajña is concluded.

2.3.1.1. They strew grass around the fires and bring down the vessels. 2.3.1.2. Having washed the vessels in the evening, he stands waiting for the cows as they approach, reciting: “These come, yielding honey; may Prajāpati and Indra cause you, O cows, to rest here” (TB 3.7.4.14–15). He addresses either the sacrificer, or a bull, or the cow-pen. 2.3.1.3. Having offered the Agnihotra, he causes the Sānnāyya milk to be milked.
2.3.1.4. He says, "Announce her when she has been approached.

2.3.1.5. When he announces that she has been approached, he then consecrates her with the mantra: "May you be free from disease through progeny, swelling with abundance, and [full of] ghee" (TB 3.7.4.15).
2.3.1.6. With the mantra, "Living, may we dwell near you who are living," he approaches the cowherd as he sits nearby.
2.3.1.7. With the formula, "Oṃ! You are the cauldron of Mātariśvan" (TS 1.1.3.b), he pushes out the embers from the Gārhapatya fire toward the north.
2.3.1.8. With the formula, "You are heaven; you are earth" (TS 1.1.3.c), he takes up the cooking pot.
2.3.1.9. With the formula, "You are the all-sustainer, by the higher name" (TS 1.1.3.d, var.), he places it over the fire.
2.3.1.10. With the formula, “Be firm; do not falter,” (TS 1.1.4h, with variation), he makes her firm upon the coals.

2.3.1.11. With the formula, “Thou art the purifier of the Vasus” (TS 1.1.3f, with variation), he places the branch-purifier with its tips pointing eastward into her opening, [saying] “having a hundred streams, a thousand streams.
2.3.1.12. Restraining his speech, he remains holding onto the pot; they bring [the water].
2.3.1.13. As he brings the milk for him, he asks, "Whom did you milk? [The response is] "That one. 2.3.1.14. [He recites: "She who possesses all life" (RV 1.1.3.k1). They indeed bring it. 2.3.1.15.
As they bring the milk for him, he asks, "Whom did you milk? [The response is] "That one."
2.3.1.16. They indeed fetch [the milk] with the verse, "She who encompasses all" (TS 1.1.3.k2).
2.3.1.17. As he brings the milk to him, he asks, "Which one did you milk? and [he replies], "That one. 2.3.1.18. [He pours it out] with the verse, "She who sustains all" (TS 1.1.3.k3).
2.3.1.19. Having recited three times, "Yield much milk for Indra; yield much milk for Indra as an oblation," he releases his speech with the words, "Give [the milk] to the calves.
2.3.1.20. If there should be only one milking, he should separate it in this very manner three times.
2.3.1.21. But if there should be many, he should cause them to be milked in this very manner.

2.3.1.22. He consecrates the droplets with the formula: “The drop has been offered, the spray has been offered” (TS 1.1.3g). 2.3.1.23. Where the cow-herder cleanses himself, he pours water into the milking vessel and says: “Svāhā to Agni, to the great firmament, to Heaven and Earth! O Agni, protect the droplets! (TS 1.1.3h–i, with variants + MS 1.1.3:2.9). Then he pours in the rinsing water with the verse: “Be united, O you who possess the cosmic order! (TS 1.1.3l, variant). [He continues: “Mixing with milk, full of waves of milk, most honey-sweet, delightful for the winning of wealth” (Cf. MS 4.1.3c:5.9; MŚS 1.1.3.32c).
2.3.1.24. With the words, “Rising, you are the heavenly world,” he causes [the fire] to shine; [he says], “Make it shine in the three worlds” (cf. p6.6). 2.3.1.25.
With the words, “O waters, you are the source of existence,” he pours water back [into the fire] with the *sruva* spoon, saying, “Make this sacrificer flourish with offspring and cattle” (cf.
p6.6). 2.3.1.26. With the words, “Rising, you are the heavenly world,” he causes [it] to shine once more; [he says], “Make it shine in the three worlds” (cf. p6.6).

2.3.1.27. With the formula, "The *rakṣas* is enclosed; the enemies are enclosed," he carries fire around [the oblation] three times from left to right (cf. ŚB 6.6). 2.3.1.28. Having thrown the illuminator (*abhidyotana*) into the fire, he establishes them with the formula, "May Indra mix you. 2.3.1.29. He should not recite [this] before it has cooled down.

2.3.1.30. When he considers it cold, he curdles the oblation with the curdling agent (*ātañcana*) while reciting: "I curdle thee, the portion of Indra, with Soma. (KS 1.3:31.2; ŚB 1.7.1.19; VS 1.4). 2.3.1.31. With the formula, "Thou art taken; for Viṣṇu thee," (TB 3.7.4.17; 3.2.3.2), he covers it with a vessel containing water, saying, "O Agni, protect the oblation. He then places it where he considers it to be secure.

2.3.1.32. In this very manner, having offered the morning *agnihotra*, he causes the *sānnāyya* milk to be milked; here he does not wait for the sun to rise, nor does he illuminate the fire, nor does he carry forth the water, nor does he anoint the sacrificial post. 2.3.1.33. Intending to pour out the oblation after the washing is finished, he sets down the sacrificial implements: the wooden sword (*sphya*), the potsherds, the *agnihotra*-ladle, the winnowing basket, the black antelope skin, the yoke-pin, the mortar, the pestle, the lower grinding stone, and the upper grinding stone. For him, they bring the materials for the rice-cake (*puroḍāśa*).
2.3.1.34. Having placed them to the west of the *gārhapatya* fire, he takes up the two strainers with the formula, "You two belong to Viṣṇu.
2.3.1.35. At the same time that he sets aside the *agnihotra* oblation, having set down the *agnihotra* pot, he pours water into it across the strainers.

2.3.1.36. Having stood up and brought those waters—measured by the distance from his mouth—from between the altar and the rubbish heap (*utkara*), he deposits them to the north of the *āhavanīya* fire.
2.3.1.37. He comes, bringing the two strainers as if slightly bent.
2.3.1.38. He turns toward his right shoulder.
2.3.1.39. With the words, "May I be able for the work of the gods" (TS 1.1.4a), he purifies both hands together with the strainers.

2.3.1.40. With the formula, "For the sake of impelling thee," he takes up the *agnihotrahavaṇī* ladle, the pot for the *caru*, and the winnowing basket. 2.3.1.41. With the formula, "The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away," he heats them over the *gārhapatya* fire.
2.3.1.42. With the formula, "I move along the wide mid-region," he goes toward half of the materials for the *puroḍāśa*.
2.3.1.43. To the west of the Gārhapatya fire, having turned toward the east and made a lap, he sits down.
2.3.1.44. Over the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśīya*), he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art the yoke-pole; injure him who injures. (TS 1.1.4d).

2.3.1.45. Having placed [the grains] upon the two strainers (*pavitre*), he recites: “O Dhur, destroy him who injures us; destroy him whom we injure. You are the most bountiful of the gods, the vessel of the oblation (*havirdhāna*). Be firm; do not falter. Let Viṣṇu step upon you. I gaze upon you with the eye of Mitra. Do not fear, do not tremble; may I not harm you. (TS 1.1.4e–h + ? 2.3.1.46.
With the formula, “Wide space for the wind” (TS 1.1.4l), he throws out a small portion from among the materials intended for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśīya*).
2.3.1.E. He takes up the offering-ladle (*sruc*) together with the two strainers.
2.3. (2.1.4) 2.3.2.1. He takes up the offering-ladle (*sruc*) together with the strainers (*pavitra*). 2.3.2.2.

Into it he pours four handfuls [of grain], saying: “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ... by the arms of the Aśvins, by the hands of Pūṣan, I pour out what is pleasing to Agni”—thus three times with the *yajus* formula, and the fourth time silently.

2.3.2.3. He pours [the grains] out with the formula, "With faith. 2.3.2.4. He takes up the pot for the *caru* together with the two strainers. 2.3.2.5. Into that [pot], he pours four handfuls [of grain] with the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ... and so on, ending with "...I pour out what is pleasing to Soma with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan. At the full moon sacrifice, he says "to Viṣṇu"; at the new moon sacrifice, he says "to Agni. He pours three times with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) and the fourth time silently.
2.3.2.6. He pours them out with the formula, "With faith. 2.3.2.7. He takes up the ladle together with the strainers. 2.3.2.8.

Over that [ladle], he pours out four handfuls with the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ... I pour out what is pleasing to Agni and Soma," at the full moon sacrifice; at the new moon sacrifice, he says, "to Indra and Agni."
2.3.2.9. For one who has not sacrificed, [he offers] with "To Indra"; for one who has sacrificed, three times indeed with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) and the fourth time silently.
2.3.2.10. At the fourth [offering], he pours in a greater amount.
2.3.2.11. As much as he leaves over, that he pours down with "With faith" (*śraddhayā*).

2.3.2.12. When the grains have been poured out, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "Agni, the Hotṛ, him I invoke here; the gods worthy of sacrifice whom we invoke here, may they come to this [sacrifice].

2.3.2.13. With the words, "Who yokes you? Let him yoke you," he gazes at the mortar and pestle. 2.3.2.14. With the words, "The potsherds which [were used] for the Gharma," they collect the potsherds, [reciting]: "O Indra and Vāyu, may those [potsherds] of Pūṣan, the ordainer, be joined together under the same vow."
2.3.2.15. With the words, “This [is] of the gods” (*TS* 1.1.4n), he touches the poured-out [grains]; with the words, “And this [is] ours together,” he touches that from which he pours them out.

2.3.2.16. With the words, “For protection from thee, not for ill-will” (*TS* 1.1.4o), having taken up both the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the grains for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśīya*), he stands up.
2.3.2.17. With the words, “May I look upon the light of heaven” (*TS* 1.1.4p), he looks around; with the words, “The light of Vaiśvānara,” he gazes at the Āhavanīya fire.
2.3.2.18. With the words, “May the doors of heaven and earth be made firm” (TS 1.1.4.q), he steps forward; [and with] “Follow the wide intermediate space” (TS 1.1.4.r). 2.3.2.19.
With the words, “I set thee in the lap of Aditi” (TS 1.1.4.s), he places the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśīya*) to the north of the *gārhapatya* fire.
2.3.2.20. With the words, “O Agni, protect the oblation” (TS 1.1.4.t), having washed the offering-spoons, he pours water into them across the strainers.
2.3.2.21. With the formula, "Purified by the mind of Viṣṇu," he wipes the two strainers.

2.3.2.22. With the formula, "May the divine Savitṛ purify you upward," using the two strainers whose tips point northward, he purifies the water with the formula, "With the flawless strainer, with the rays of the sun, O Vasu."

2.3.2.23. With the verse, “O divine waters, you who flow forward” (TS 1.1.5b–c), he sprinkles [the grains] three times, saying: “O you who flow forward, lead this sacrifice forward; place the lord of the sacrifice at the head. You who seek the gods—Indra chose you for the slaying of Vṛtra; you chose Indra for the slaying of Vṛtra. 2.3.2.24. With the formula, “You are sprinkled” (TS 1.1.5d), he sprinkles the water three times with water. 2.3.2.25.

With the formula, “I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni,” he sprinkles the grains intended for the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*). He says, “Acceptable to such-and-such, acceptable to such-and-such,” according to whichever deity they belong to.

2.3.2.26. With the formula, "May they be purified for the divine rite" (TS 1.1.5f), he sprinkles the vessels while they are turned face upwards; with "The vessels for the sacrifice to the gods," he sprinkles the mortar and pestle; he sprinkles the potsherds. 2.3.2.27.

Having placed the *prokṣaṇī* water-pitcher to the east of the *gārhapatya* fire, and having taken up the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the materials for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśīya*), he goes to the middle of the mortar.
2.3.2.28. Having set down the materials for the sacrificial cake, he takes up the black antelope skin with the formula, "Thou art the skin of Aditi" (TS 1.1.5h1).

2.3.2.29. He shakes [the mortar] with the mantra: "The demon is shaken off; the enemies are shaken off. (TS 1.1.5.g) 2.3.2.30. With the mantra: "May the earth recognize you," (TS 1.1.5.h²) he spreads out a skin with its neck facing westward and its hair side upward.

2.3.2.31. Having touched water, he places the mortar upon it with its opening facing westward, using the mantra: "Thou art the wooden pressing-vessel," (TS 1.1.5.i) and then [he says]: "May the skin of Aditi recognize you; make firm the earth. (TS 1.1.5.j)

2.3.2.32. With the formula, "Thou art the body of Agni, the release of speech" (*TS* 1.1.5k–l), he pours four handfuls [of grain] while saying, "I take you for the feast of the gods, for the release of speech. 2.3.2.33. With the formula, "Thou art the great pressing-stone" (*TS* 1.1.5m), he takes up the pestle.
2.3.2.34. With the formula, "Having pressed upwards," he places [the pestle] down, saying, "Do thou prepare this oblation for the gods; prepare it well, prepare it thoroughly. (*TS* 1.1.5n)
2.3.2.35. With the formula, “O preparer of the oblation, come! he strikes three times, saying, “O preparer of the oblation, come! O preparer of the oblation, come! 2.3.2.36.

Having released his speech with the preparer of the oblation and having placed the *śamyā* pegs to the south facing east, he causes the grain to resound with the wooden sword (*sphya*) three times, saying, “Proclaim food! Proclaim strength! (TS 1.1.5.o). 2.3.2.37. Having removed the husks with the formula, “Speak with splendor; may we conquer host after host! (TS 1.1.5.p–r), he takes up the winnowing basket (*śūrpa*) with the formula, “Thou art increased by rain. (TS 1.1.5.s).

2.3.2.38. With the mantra, “May those increased by rain come toward you” (*TS* 1.1.5), he pours [the grain] out toward the north. 2.3.2.39. Having sat down and turned toward the north, he winnows [the grain].

2.3.2.40. Having threshed [the grain], saying, “The *rakṣas* is winnowed away; the enemies are winnowed away,” he pours the husks below the black antelope skin to the west of the mortar, saying, “You are the portion of the *rakṣases*; here I lead this *rakṣas* down into the lowest darkness—him who hates us and whom we hate, here I lead him down into the lowest darkness” (*TS* 1.1.5t–u).
2.3.2.41. Having touched water, he separates [the grains] with the formula: "May Vāyu separate you" (TS 1.1.5v). 2.3.2.42.
He touches those that have been separated with the formula: "Be purified for the gods. 2.3.2.43. While pouring [them into the mortar], he says: "Announce them as having been thrice-pounded."
(2.2.1) 2.4.1.1. With the formula, "Thou art bold; bestow the *brahman*," (TS 1.1.7a), he takes up the fire-stirring stick (*upaveṣa*).
2.4.1.2. With the formula, "O Agni, drive away the raw-eating Agni," (TS 1.1.7b1), he turns away two glowing coals.
2.4.1.3. With the formula, "Of these two, drive away the flesh-eater with the *ṅiṣ*," he pushes back one [of the two stones] toward the south.
2.4.1.4. With the formula, "Bring hither the one that goes to the sacrifice of the gods," he turns the other [stone] back.

2.4.1.5. Upon it, he places the middle potsherd of the eight-pot-sherd cake with the formula, "Thou art firm; make firm the earth! Make firm the *brahman*, make firm the *kṣatra*, make firm the subjects, make firm wealth, make firm the increase of wealth, make firm the kinsmen for the sacrificer! (TS 1.1.7d var).
2.4.1.6. Therefore, he should not step over it before the embers have been removed.

2.4.1.7. He silently places an ember upon it, or [he says]: "Do not burn the head of the earth. 2.4.1.8. With the formula, "Thou art the support; make firm the intermediate space" (TS 1.1.7.1), he places it behind [the fire], [saying]: "Make firm the Brahman, make firm the Kṣatra; make firm the kinsmen for the sacrificer."

2.4.1.9. With the formula, “Thou art the support of heaven; make firm,” (TS 1.1.7f1), having enclosed it with the northern [enclosing-stick], he places it in the east, saying, “Make firm the *brahman*; make firm for the sacrificer. 2.4.1.10. With the formula, “Thou art the law (*dharma*); make firm the quarters,” (TS 1.1.7g1), having carried it around by the east, he places it in the south, saying, “Make firm the *brahman*; make firm the kinsmen for the sacrificer. 2.4.1.11. With the formula, “Make firm all the regions and the quarters,” he places the *pradhika* brick in the north [cf. BŚS 1.8:11.8; Caland, Śrautasūtra of the Āpastambins, Part I, p. 164].
2.4.1.12. He should make the other [layer] well-prepared with the formula: “O Brahman, make firm; make the kinsmen firm for the sacrificer. 2.4.1.13.
With the formula, “You are piled, you are well-piled” (TS 1.1.7h), he piles the *pariciti* bricks. 2.4.1.14.

Having turned away, he covers them with embers with the formula, “From all directions I pile you; make the Brahman firm, make the Kṣatra firm, make the subjects firm, make wealth firm, make the increase of wealth firm, make the kinsmen firm for the sacrificer,” and with the formula, “Be heated by the heat of the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases,” he covers them with embers.

2.4.1.15. Having drawn out embers to the north and placed the *caru*-pot upon them, he pours water into it across the strainers; in this very same manner, he arranges the potsherds for the eleven-pot offering. 2.4.1.16. Having washed the rice grains intended for the *caru*, he cooks them.
2.4.1.17. With the formula, "Thou art the skin of Aditi," he takes up the black antelope skin.

2.4.1.18. He shakes [the mortar] with the mantra: "Shaken off is the demon; shaken off are the enemies" (TS 1.1.6a). 2.4.1.19. With the mantra, "May the earth recognize you" (TS 1.1.6b), he spreads out a hide with its neck facing westward and the hair side upward.

2.4.1.20. Having touched water, he places the lower millstone upon it with the mantra, "Thou art the bowl belonging to the mountain" (TS 1.1.6d), and [he places the upper stone] with the mantra, "May the skin of Aditi recognize you; make firm the earth" (TS 1.1.6e).

2.4.1.21. With the formula, “Thou art the pillar of heaven; make firm the mid-region,” he pushes the *śamyā* peg towards the north from behind. 2.4.1.22. With the formula, “Thou art the lower millstone, daughter of the mountain; may the mountain-born [upper stone] recognize thee;

make firm the sky,” he places the upper millstone upon the lower one. 2.4.1.23. With the formula, “Thou art grain; satisfy the gods,” he pours four handfuls [of grain] onto it, saying, “Satisfy the sacrifice, satisfy the lord of the sacrifice, satisfy me, the performer of the sacrifice.”

2.4.1.24. With the words, "For out-breath thee," he crushes [the grain] toward the east; with "For diffused breath thee," toward the south; with "For in-breath thee," toward himself; and with "For up-breath thee," he grinds [it] toward the north. With the words, "May you two unite along a long extension," 2.4.1.25. "For life yours," he looks at his two arms. 2.4.1.26.
With the words, "May the divine Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive them," he looks at the fallen rice grains.
2.4.1.27. "With unimpaired sight I gaze upon you for the sake of good offspring"—with these words they form the flour-mixture [cf.

*PŚS* 1.21, etc.]. 2.4.1.28. Taking the two strainers (*pavitra*), he pours them into the vessel and says: "Bring [the water] from the *praṇītā*s; spread out the *veda* grass. 2.4.1.29. They do this: he brings [the water] from the *praṇītā*s with the *sruva*-ladle, approaches, spreads out the *veda* grass, and performs the purification (*mārjana*).

2.4.1.30. Having sat down to the west of the Gārhapatya fire, turned toward the east, with the formula, “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ” (TS 1.1.6f), he pours the flour together with two strainers whose tips point northward, saying: “With the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I pour together what is pleasing to Agni, what is pleasing to [so-and-so], what is pleasing to [so-and-so]”—thus according to whichever deities the offerings belong.

2.4.1.31. With the mantra, "The waters have come together with the plants" (TS 1.1.8b–c), he pours water across the strainer using the *sruva* ladle, saying, "O wealthy ones, united with the moving plants, flow together—sweet with the sweet. 2.4.1.32. Having poured more water, he causes it to overflow three times with water, saying, "You are born from the waters," and "Be purified by the waters for our well-being."

2.4.1.33. With the formula, “I mix [the grains] for the people’s enjoyment” (TS 1.1.8e–f), he mixes them; with the formula, “Pleasant to Agni, pleasant to so-and-so, pleasant to so-and-so,” according to the deities to whom they belong.
2.4.1.34. Having ground the flour, he forms a lump with the formula, “Thou art the head of Makha” (TS 1.1.8g).
2.4.1.35. He separates the two portions with the formula, “Separate yourselves according to your respective shares.”

2.4.1.36. With the formula, "I drive away the face of this attacking army," he drives away the embers from the eight-potsherd [offering] with the *veda* grass-bundle, moving them away from him; he should not drive them toward himself. 2.4.1.37.
With the formula, "Thou art the Gharma, the life of all," he places [the vessel] over the fire.
2.4.1.38. With the formula, "Spread wide; may the lord of the sacrifice spread wide for thee," he spreads out all the potsherds.
2.4.1.39. He pours the *caru* across the strainer.

2.4.1.40. In this very same manner, he places the cake on eleven potsherds upon the fire. 2.4.1.41. Having poured water into a vessel, he causes the skin [of the rice] to be taken up three times with the formula, “Take hold of the skin,” and [he adds], “May Agni not injure your skin. (TS 1.1.8.k + ?)

2.4.1.42. With the formula, "Thou art the milk of the great ones," he pours out the clarified butter across the strainer, [saying]: "Thou art the essence of the waters and the plants; of that milk of thine, swelling, inexhaustible, and undiminished, I pour out for the sacrifice to the gods.
2.4.1.43. Having pushed out embers to the north, he places it over the fire.
2.4.1.44. He sets down curd for him as the *sānnāyya* offering.

2.4.1.45. Then, having taken a glowing coal with either an iron ladle or a fire-stirring stick (*upaveṣa*) from the cooked [offering], he carries fire around it three times by moving to the right, saying: "The *rakṣas* is excluded; the enemies are excluded" (*TS* 1.1.8). 2.4.1.46. Having returned the coal [to the fire], he releases his speech, saying: "Cook without burning! (*TB* 3.2.8). 2.4.1.47.
