2.4.2.1. He releases his speech with the words, "Cooking without burning, cook! (cf. ŚB 3.2.8.7), [saying] "Stir the sacrificial porridge. 2.4.2.2. With the words, "May the god Savitṛ cook you" (TS 1.1.8m), he touches the oblations one after another, [reciting] "Upon the highest vault of heaven" (TS 1.1.8n).
2.4.2.3. With the words, "May Agni not burn up your body" (TS 1.1.8n), he fans them down with blades of grass.

2.4.2.4. With the formula, "O Agni, accept the *brahman*," he covers [the altar] with ashes, saying, "The sacrifice is tireless; the sacrificer is tireless; the cattle of the sacrificer are tireless. 2.4.2.5.

Having silently touched the oblations in their proper order with the *veda*-grass-bundle, and having taken the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the washing-water, he goes to the middle of the Āhavanīya fire.
2.4.2.6. Inside the altar, he draws one line on the northern shoulder; two lines outside the altar.
2.4.2.7. With the formula, "Svāhā to Oneness," he pours [the water] within the altar; with "Svāhā to Twoness, Svāhā to Threeness," he pours it outside the altar. 2.4.2.8.

Having silently heated [the vessel] with a firebrand, having wiped it out, having cleansed it, and having washed it, as well as the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he places them within the altar. 2.4.2.9. To the south, the Brahman and the sacrificer sit down; behind them, the Āgnīdhra, turned toward the east, sits down on the rubbish-heap (*utkara*) with his right knee bent.
2.4.2.10. With the words, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ," he takes up the wooden sword (*sphya*), [adding] "with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan" (cf.

TS 1.1.9a; TS 2.6.4.1; TB 3.2.9.1a; BŚS 1.11). 2.4.2.11. With the words, "Thou art hundred-edged, made of wood," he wipes it with sacrificial grass (*barhis*), [continuing] "the weapon against the hater; thou art Indra’s right arm, thousand-edged, hundred-fold sharp; thou art Vāyu, sharp-edged; do not harm me, at the impulse of the god Savitṛ" (TS 2.6.4.1 + 1.1.9b–c).
2.4.2.12. With the words, “May humans perform their work,” he places a blade of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with its tip pointing north within the altar (*antarvedi*).

2.4.2.13. With the words, “O earth, place of sacrifice to the gods; may I not harm your root, O herb,” he strikes [the ground] with the wooden sword (*sphya*). 2.4.2.14. With the words, “Go to the fold, the cow-pen,” he carries half [of the grass] to the rubbish heap (*utkara*).

2.4.2.15. With the words, “May the sky rain for you” (TS 1.1.9.g), he gazes at the altar. 2.4.2.16. With the words, “Bind him, O God Savitṛ” (TS 1.1.9.h), he presses down [the grass] on the rubbish-heap (utkara), saying: “In the furthest distance, with a hundred nooses—him who hates us and whom we hate—do not let him go from there. 2.4.2.17. With the words, “I have bound him away” (TS 1.1.9.i), he strikes a second time, saying: “From the earth’s place of sacrifice; O Earth, place of sacrifice, may I not harm the root of your plant. (Cf. TS 1.1.9.i and n; TS 1.1.9.d).

2.4.2.18. With the words, “Go to the cow-pen, the place of cattle,” he carries half of the rubbish-heap (*utkara*). With the words, “May the sky rain for you,” he looks back at the altar (*vedi*). With the words, “Bind him, O God Savitṛ,” he presses [the clod] down upon the rubbish-heap with the formula: “In the furthest distance, with a hundred nooses—him who hates us and whom we hate—do not release him from there.
2.4.2.19. With the words, “Let not your *araru* leap up to heaven,” he strikes for the third time.

2.4.2.20. With the formula, “From the earth, the place of sacrifice to the gods; O Earth, O place of sacrifice to the gods, may I not harm the root of your plant,” he carries half of the *utkara* heap [of earth] while saying, “Go to the fold, the stall for cattle. With the formula, “May the sky rain for you,” he gazes at the *vedi*. With the formula, “Bind him, O God Savitṛ,” he presses it down upon the *utkara* heap, saying, “In the furthest distance, with a hundred nooses—him who hates us and whom we hate—do not release him from there.
2.4.2.21. He carries the fourth portion silently, together with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).

2.4.2.22. With the formula, “May the Vasus enclose you with the Gāyatrī metre,” he encloses the altar from the south, extending it eastward, using the wooden sword (*sphya*). With the formula, “May the Rudras enclose you with the Triṣṭubh metre,” [he encloses it] from behind, extending it northward. With the formula, “May the Ādityas enclose you with the Jagatī metre,” [he encloses it] from the north, extending it eastward.

2.4.2.23. With the formula, “O men, come and prepare this altar,” he digs up [the earth]. With the formula, “On the height of heaven, on the navel of the earth, so that this sacrificer may not come to harm” (cf. TB 3.7.7.13–14; BŚS 1.11:15.7).
2.4.2.24. He says "Hara" to the Āgnīdhra. 2.4.2.25. Having carried away the earth that has been dug up three times, he wipes it with his hand.
2.4.2.26. Then he says, "O Brahman, I shall perform the second tracing of the altar."

2.4.2.27. With the formula, “Thou art the seat of Ṛta” (TS 1.1.9u), he encloses the altar from the south with the wooden sword (sphya), directed eastward; with “Thou art the seat of Satya,” from the west, directed northward; and with “Thou art the seat of Dharma,” from the north, directed eastward. 2.4.2.28.
With the formula, “Thou art dhā, thou art svadhā” (TS 1.1.9v), he smoothes the altar from the west with the wooden sword.

2.4.2.29. “*urvī cāsi...* ‘...the wise ones, looking toward them, sacrifice’” (TS 1.1.9.w–x). Having propped [the post] crosswise within the *vedī* with the wooden sword (*sphya*), he issues the command: “Set down the sprinkling waters (*prokṣaṇī*); place the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmā-barhis*) nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon (*sruva*) and the offering-spoons (*sruk*); gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter (*ājya*). 2.4.2.31. Having performed the purification (*mārjana*), the *Āgnīdhra*, having poured the sprinkling waters along the track of the wooden sword, sets them down, saying: “I set thee down in the breath of so-and-so. (TB 3.2.9.15.j; BŚS 1.11:15.18–16.2)

2.4.2.32. With the wooden sword (sphya), he strikes north of the rubbish-heap (utkara); the sacrificer meditates upon whomsoever he hates. 2.4.2.33. Having touched water, having purified himself, and having washed the wooden sword, he returns and cleanses the offering-ladles (sruk) with the trimmed fringes of the altar-grass (vedaparivāsana). 2.4.2.34.
"Thou art the ladle, unassailable, the subduer of rivals"—with these words, he takes up the small spoon (sruva).
“Thou art the dipping-spoon (sruva), unassailable, overcoming rivals,” with these words he takes up the sruva-ladle.
2.4.3.2. “The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away,” with these words (TS 1.1.10a) he heats it over the Gārhapatya fire.

2.4.3.3. He wipes [the ladle] with the formula: “May I not wipe away life and breath” (TS 1.1.10d var), and [he adds]: “I wipe you, the vigorous one, the overcomer of rivals. 2.4.3.4. Having heated it three times on the inside and once from below, he hands it over.
2.4.3.5. With the formula: “You are the Juhū-ladle, unassailable, the overcomer of rivals,” he takes up the Juhū-ladle.
2.4.3.6. He heats [the ladle] over the Gārhapatya fire with the formula: “The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away. 2.4.3.7.
He cleanses it with the formula: “May I not wipe away my sight or my hearing,” and [with the formula]: “I cleanse thee, the vigorous one, the subduer of rivals. 2.4.3.8.
Having heated it three times on the inside and once underneath, he hands it over.
2.4.3.9. “Thou art the *upabhṛt* ladle, unassailable, overcoming rivals,” with these words he takes up the *upabhṛt*.
2.4.3.10. “The *rakṣas* is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away,” with these words he heats it over the *gārhapatya* fire.
2.4.3.11. “May I not wipe away offspring and the womb,” with these words he cleanses it, saying, “I cleanse thee, the vigorous one, who overcomes rivals.”
2.4.3.12. Having heated them three times on the inside and once underneath, he hands them over after having indeed scorched them.
2.4.3.13. With the formula, "Firm art thou, unassailable, overcoming rivals," he takes up the *dhruvā* ladle.
2.4.3.14. With the formula, "Scorched is the demon, scorched are the enemies," he heats it over the *gārhapatya* fire.
2.4.3.15. He wipes [the ladle] with the formula, “May I not wipe away wealth from the cow-pen” (TS 1.1.10.c), and [he adds], “I wipe thee, the vigorous one, the subduer of rivals.
2.4.3.16. Having heated them thus three times on the inside and once below, he hands them over while they are still hot.
2.4.3.17. Having silently taken the *prāśitraharaṇa* vessel, he heats it over the *gārhapatya* fire with the formula, “The demon is burnt up; the enemies are burnt up.”
2.4.3.18. He cleanses [the ladle] with the formula, "May I not wipe away the color from the form," and [again] with, "I cleanse you, the vigorous one, the subduer of rivals. 2.4.3.19.
Having thus cleansed it three times on the inside and once below, he heats it over the fire and hands it back.

2.4.3.20. Having touched the *vedaparivāsanā* grass-bundles with water, he throws them away in a place where no one walks. 2.4.3.21. Having taken the *sruca* ladles [and placed them] behind the *utkara* heap, and having spread out grass-blades, they set them down one after another in order, turning toward the north.
2.4.3.22. Having returned and sat down behind the *gārhapatya* fire, he girdles the wife with the formula: "Aiming for goodwill—for the sake of good action. (TS 1.1.10.e)
2.4.3.23. With the verse, “*Suprajasas tvā vayam* (TS 1.1.10f), he makes her recite this secret formula (*upaniṣad*): “*Śupatnīr upasedima adabdhāso adābhyam*. 2.4.3.24.

With the verse, “*Indrāṇīvāvidhavā bhūyāsam*,” he makes her recite the following secret formula: “*Aditir iva suputrā asthūri tvāgne gārhapatyānuniṣadeyam*. 2.4.3.25. With the verse, “*Payasvatīr oṣadhayaḥ* (TS 1.1.10g), he causes her to drink water through the strainer, saying: “*Payasvad vīrudhām payo apāṃ va saṃsṛja*.”

2.4.3.26. Having performed the purification with the formula, “O Agni, lord of vows...,” he places a fuel-stick on the fire with the formula, “I shall perform the vow; may I be able to do so; may it be successful for me, svāhā! (TS 1.1.10h + svāhā). 2.4.3.27. With the formula, “Thou art ghee,” he makes her look at the ghee with the formula, “I gaze upon thee with unimpaired vision; thou art the sustainer of my desires for progeny; for the sake of good offspring. (TS 1.1.10k2). 2.4.3.28. With the formula, “Thou art splendor; follow after splendor,” he takes up the ghee and carries it forward with the formula, “May Vāyu protect thee from the intermediate space; may Sūrya [protect thee] from heaven. (TS 1.1.10l1).
2.4.3.29. With the words, "O Agni, let not thy heat burn me," he places [the vessel] over the Āhavanīya fire.
2.4.3.30. If the wife is sitting nearby, with the words, "Sit for the gods, for strength," he sets down the *prokṣaṇī* waters to the north.

2.4.3.31. With the words, "Thou art the tongue of Agni," they both look at it through the intervening space, saying, "A good being for the gods; for every station, for every sacrificial formula (*yajus*), become [auspicious] for the gods."
2.4.3.32. “Come, O sacrificer,” he says. 2.4.3.33.

The sacrificer walks around to the east of the Āhavanīya fire, the *praṇītā* waters to the north, the rubbish heap (*utkara*) to the south, and the offering spoons (*srucaḥ*) to the north; having stepped across to the west of the altar (*vedi*), he turns toward the north and sits down to the south.
2.4.3.34. With the formula, “Thou art ghee” (TS 1.6.1.b), he causes him to recite over the ghee: “Thou art truth, the overseer of truth; may I partake of thee.”
2.4.3.35. With the words, “O *asava*, protect that for me,” he gazes at his own reflection.

2.4.3.36. With the formula, “Thou art splendor” (*tejo ’si*), he purifies the clarified butter with two strainers whose tips point toward the north, [reciting]: “Thou art brilliance, thou art light, thou art immortality; with uplifted heat, possessing true vigor. 2.4.3.37. He takes up both the *sruva* and the *juhū* ladles.
2.4.3.38. Into that [ladle] he takes four spoonfuls with the formula: “Thou art brilliance, thou art the abode, the beloved, unassailable place of sacrifice for the gods.
2.4.3.39. Having wiped it, he hands it over. 2.4.3.40. He takes up the *upabhṛt* ladle.
2.4.3.41. Into that [ladle] he takes four full *sruva*-ladles with the formula: "Thou art brilliance; thou art the abode, the beloved of the gods, the inviolable place of sacrifice.
2.4.3.42. He takes another four half-*sruva* ladles silently.
2.4.3.43. Having wiped it, he hands it over.

2.4.3.44. He takes up the *dhruvā* ladle. 2.4.3.45. Into it he pours four spoonfuls [of clarified butter] with the formula: "Thou art immortality; thou art a foundation; thou art the beloved, unassailable place of sacrifice of the gods. 2.4.3.46.
At the fourth [pouring], he pours in more.
2.4.3.47. He leaves a remnant from the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings. 2.4.3.48. Having wiped it, he hands it over.

2.4.3.49. Having placed the butter-pot together with the *sruva*-ladle behind the altar, and having taken up the *prokṣaṇī* sprinkling waters, he silently sprinkles the supporting surface (*dharuṇa*).

2.4.3.50. Having stood up, he sprinkles the faggot after loosening it with the formula: "Thou art the black one; standing in the cleft, I sprinkle thee, acceptable to Agni" (TS 1.1.11a). He sprinkles the altar with: "Thou art the altar; I sprinkle thee, acceptable to the sacrificial grass" (TS 1.1.11b), and the sacrificial grass with: "Thou art the sacrificial grass; I sprinkle thee, acceptable to the ladles" (TS 1.1.11c). 2.4.3.51. Having placed that which has been sprinkled within the altar with its knot toward the east, he sprinkles it with: "For heaven thee, for the intermediate space thee, for earth thee" (TS 1.1.11d).

2.4.3.52. He silently sprinkles [the water] over the knot from the front; he silently pours it out behind [the altar], and [he pours it out] on the southern buttock [of the altar] with the formula: “May the world, the seat of the fathers, be purified” (TS 1.1.11d). 2.4.3.53. With the formula: “Go to the earth with strength; Svadhā to the fathers; be wide for those who sit on the sacrificial grass” (TS 1.1.11e), he pours it out continuously toward the northern buttock. Having poured it out behind himself and to the east of the rubbish-heap (utkara), he pushes the ladle across toward the north. 2.4.3.54.
Having untied the sacrificial grass (barhis), he takes up the prastara-bunch together with the strainers from the front with the formula: “Thou art Viṣṇu’s tuft” (TS 1.1.11g).
2.4.3.55. He hands it to the sacrificer, or he places it in the hand of the Brahman priest, or he holds it in his own left hand.
2.4.3.56. Having made a firm binding at the tip, he lays it down on the southern buttock of the altar.

2.4.3.57. With the formula, “O divine sacrificial grass,” he covers it with a handful of grass, saying, “I spread thee, O soft-to-the-touch, as a good seat for the gods. (The term *devabarhis* is formed according to Pāṇini 1.1.11.)
With the words, "Wide for the sacrifice," he scatters three handfuls of grass toward the east with the formula, "Wide for the sacrificer, wide for the lord of the sacrifice.
With the words, "Strew the sacrificial grass," he releases his speech.
2.4.4.1. With the words, "Strew the sacrificial grass," he releases his speech.
2.4.4.2. They strew the threefold sacrificial grass.
2.4.4.3. Having taken the prastara-bunch so that it is not visible beyond [the altar], and having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks.

2.4.4.4. With the formula, "Thou art the Gandharva Viśvāvasu" (TS 1.1.11i-l, var), he lays the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) down; with the formula, "Thou art the enclosing-stick for the protection of the sacrificer from every leader; be thou praised, O praised one," [he lays] the southern one. 2.4.4.5. With the formula, "Thou art the right arm of Indra," [he lays] the southernmost [enclosing-stick]; with the formula, "Thou art the enclosing-stick for the protection of the sacrificer from every leader; be thou praised, O praised one. 2.4.4.6. With the formula, "May Mitra and Varuṇa enclose thee from the north," [he lays] the northernmost [enclosing-stick]; with the formula, "By the firm law, thou art the enclosing-stick for the protection of the sacrificer from every leader; be thou praised, O praised one."

2.4.4.7. With the mantra, “May Śūrya protect you from the east” (TS 1.1.11m, n var), he places a fuel-stick on the south side: “O Sage, we kindle thee, the inviter to the sacrifice, the brilliant one, O Agni, the great one at the rite, in the highest firmament—svāhā!

(TS 1.6.2a). 2.4.4.8. He places [a fuel-stick] on the north side silently. 2.4.4.9. Over the middle enclosing stick, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: “Thou art firm; may I be firm among my kinsmen” (TS 1.6.2a–c), and “The wise, perceiving, the finder of wealth” (TS 1.6.2d).

2.4.4.10. With the formula, “Thou art fierce; may I be fierce among my kinsmen,” he touches the southern enclosing-stick (*paridhi*); with “Fierce, a perceiver, a winner of wealth,” [he touches the middle one]. 2.4.4.11. With the formula, “Thou art overcoming; may I be overcoming among my kinsmen,” he touches the northern enclosing-stick; with “Overcoming, a perceiver, a winner of wealth,” [he touches the middle one]. 2.4.4.12. Having touched the middle enclosing-stick with the formula, “I yoke thee with the divine *brahman*,” he places a fuel-stick (*samidh*) upon it with the formula, “For this oblation—[weaving for thee, O Agni, svāhā]”—(TS 1.6.2d + *agne svāhā*).

2.4.4.13. Having come and sat down to the west of the altar, facing east, he places [the two blades of grass] across inside the altar with their tips pointing north, saying: "You are the restrainers of the people. 2.4.4.14.
Upon those two, he places the *prastara* (grass-bunch) as the northern purifier, saying: "You are the seat of the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas. 2.4.4.15.
He should not brush that [prastara] away with his left hand.
2.4.4.16. With the words, "Thou art ghee-dripping," he takes up the *juhū* ladle.
2.4.4.17. With the words, "Heaven by birth, the *juhū* by name, dear to the gods by thy dear name, sit in the dear seat," he places the *juhū* upon the *prastara* grass-bundle.
2.4.4.18. He should not push those [blades] aside with his right hand.
2.4.4.19. With the words, "Thou art Ghr̥tācī," he takes up the *upabhṛt* [ladle].

2.4.4.20. With the words, "By the intermediate space as thy birthplace, O *upabhṛt*, by name; beloved of the gods by thy dear name, sit in the dear seat," he places the *upabhṛt* to the north of the *juhū*. 2.4.4.21. He should push it back slightly with his left hand and not let go of it.
2.4.4.22. With the formula, “Thou art Ghr̥tācī,” he takes up the *dhruvā* ladle.
2.4.4.23. With the formula, “Firm by birth, firm by name, dear to the gods by thy dear name, sit in the dear seat,” he places the *dhruvā* to the north of the *upabhṛt*. 2.4.4.24.

Having taken the vessel for clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*) together with the *sruva* spoon, having moved it slightly further back as it were, and having returned and sat down behind the *gārhapatya* fire facing eastward, he sets out the sacrificial oblations (*havīṃṣi*) one after another, having first spread a base of butter (*upastīrṇa*) and then poured butter over them (*abhighārita*).
2.4.4.25. He anoints the potsherds. 2.4.4.26. Having counted them, he removes them from the fire.
2.4.4.27. Having poured clarified butter over the sacrificial oblations, they bring them forward.

2.4.4.28. To the east, he places the *juhū* ladle and the cake on eight potsherds (*aṣṭākapāla*). 2.4.4.29. To the north of that, the rice-porridge (*caru*); to the north of that, the cake on eleven potsherds; on the southern hip of the altar, the curd for the *sānnāyya* offering; on the northern hip, the boiled milk. 2.4.4.30.
Standing to the south, he undertakes the vow (*vrata*).

2.4.4.31. With the mantra, “The plants are full of milk” (TS 1.5.10.g), he sips water across the strainer, [reciting] “Full of milk is the milk of the plants; mix it together” (TS 1.5.10.h). 2.4.4.32.

Having performed the ritual purification with the mantra, “O Agni, Lord of Vows” (TS 1.5.10.h), he places a fuel-stick on the fire, [reciting] “I shall perform the vow; may it be successful, svāhā! (TS 1.5.10.h + svāhā). 2.4.4.33. Having returned, he touches the offering-spoons with the mantra, “They have settled firmly” (TS 1.5.10.i): “In the womb of Truth, in the world of good deeds—protect them, O Viṣṇu! Protect the sacrifice! Protect the lord of the sacrifice! Protect me, the performer of the sacrifice! (TS 1.5.10.i).

2.4.4.34. With the formula, “Whatever of this sacrifice of mine may be spoiled, O Agni,” he touches the oblations in their proper order, [adding] “or whatever [of the clarified butter] may spill in the lap [of the altar], Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Suvar Om Vāk” (TS 1.6.2e,f + Om Vāk). 2.4.4.35. He recites the Caturhotṛ formulas over the *dhruvā* ladle.
2.5.1.1. "Recite for Agni as he is being kindled," so he says.
2.5.1.2. At each *praṇava* (the syllable *om*), he places three fuel-sticks upon [the fire], both at the setting down [of the ladle] and at the *praṇava*. 2.5.1.3.
From this point forward, the Adhvaryu seeks to encompass [the fire] with a fuel-stick while reciting the verse: "O Agni, well-kindled, you have been offered oblations."

2.5.1.4. He leaves over a piece of the fuel-stick. 2.5.1.5. When he recognizes [the sound] with the words, “Offer! Pay homage!”—then he fans the fire three times with the *veda*-grass-bundle, saying, “Upward, O Agni, for those who attack us!
2.5.1.6. With the *sruva*-ladle, he pours the *āghāra* libation from the top of the fuel-sticks toward the south, across [the fire], mentally [reciting]: “To Prajāpati, svāhā!”

2.5.1.7. Then he says, "O Agnīdh, cleanse the fires thrice each! Having taken hold of the non-bound *sphya* [sacrificial wooden sword], he cleanses the fires three times: the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*), three times the southern half, three times the northern half, and three times the fire itself (cf.

TB 3.3.7.3–4d). 2.5.1.8. With the mantra, "Thou art the world; spread thyself out" (TS 1.1.12a,b), he pays homage to the two offering-ladles (*sruc*). With the mantra, "O Agni, O Sacrificer, this is homage," 2.5.1.9. With the mantra, "O Juhū, come! Agni calls thee for the sacrifice to the gods" (TS 1.1.12c-d), he takes up the Juhū ladle.

2.5.1.10. "O Upabhṛt, come; the god Savitṛ calls you for the sacrifice to the gods," [with these words] he takes hold of the Upabhṛt. 2.5.1.11. "May they two be well-guided and full of ghee for me today," [with these words] he joins the two ladles together. 2.5.1.12.
"O Agni and Viṣṇu, may I not step between you," [with these words] he steps across, [and says] "Be parted; do not cause me harm."

2.5.1.13. Having stepped across, he mutters: "O Viṣṇu, may I stand in thy station, where Indra standing performed heroic deeds; there may I perform heroic deeds. (TS 1.1.12h,i) 2.5.1.14. [He offers] with the verse: "The sacrifice is successful, rising up, touching the sky. (TS 1.1.12k, var. 2.5.1.15.
Having touched the middle enclosing-stick, he pours the second libation continuously with: "The sacrifice of the Lord of Sacrifice is uninjured; to Indra of great luster, svāhā! (TS 1.1.12l-m, var.)

2.5.1.16. Stepping across from the south toward the north, while holding the two offering-spoons obliquely and not allowing them to touch each other, he recites: “O Agni, protect me from evil conduct; grant me a share in good conduct” (TS 1.1.12.0; cf. TB 3.7.9.7). 2.5.1.17.

Having stepped across, he anoints the *dhruvā* with the *juhū* while reciting: “May light be united with light; may the oblation be united with the oblation; may the lord of the sacrifice be united with his blessings” (TB 3.3.7.10–11).

2.5.1.18. Having set down the two offering-ladles (*srucau*) in their respective places, and having taken the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and a wooden splinter (*śakala*), he stands to the north and calls for the announcement (*āśrāvayati*) for the *pravara* (the choosing of the priests). Taking the wooden sword (*sphya*), the *āgnīdhra* priest stands behind him and touches him. 2.5.1.19. Holding the cords that bind the fuel (*idhmasannahanāni*) upon the wooden sword, he calls for the announcement; [the Adhvaryu] says, "O, announce! (*o śrāvaya*). 2.5.1.20. "May the divine Agni, the Hotṛ, sacrifice to the gods—he who is wise and discerning. Like Manu, like Bharata, like such-and-such [a sage], and like the Brahman, may he bring them hither. May the Brahmins be the promoters of this sacrifice. With these words, he chooses the Hotṛ.
2.5.1.21. He says to him, "What is your name? and he declares his name. 2.5.1.22.
He throws a wooden splinter into the Āhavanīya fire, saying, "Such-and-such a man.
2.5.1.23. As is the name of the Hotṛ, so he says, "Sit down, O Hotṛ!"
2.5.1.24. He hides the sacrificial grass right upon the sacrificial grass.
2.5.1.25. The Hotṛ sits down.
2.5.1.26. When he recognizes [the signal]: "O Adhvaryu, take up the ladle full of ghee"—then [he acts].

Then he joins his palms in reverence, saying: "O Aśvins, the two Adhvaryus; O Brāhmaṇas, the Praśāstṛs; homage be unto you! (2.5.1.27). Having taken up the two offering-spoons, the Adhvaryu steps across [the altar], saying: "O, cause [the Agnīdh] to announce! and "Recite the offering-verse for the kindling-sticks! (2.5.1.28).
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering behind [the altar] at the front of the kindling-sticks, saying: "Recite! Recite! (2.5.1.29).

2.5.1.29. He performs five fore-offerings (*prayāja*). At the fourth [fore-offering], he pours half [of the butter] from the *upabhṛt* ladle [into the *juhu*]; at the fifth, he pours all [the remaining butter] from the *upabhṛt*. 2.5.1.30. Having performed the fore-offerings and stepped across, he bastes the *dhruvā* ladle; then the cake on eight potsherds; then the porridge; then the cake on eleven potsherds; then the curd for the *sānnāyya*; then the boiled milk in the *upabhṛt* ladle. 2.5.1.31. Finally, he performs the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*).
2.5.1.32. Saying, "Recite for Agni," he takes four portions of clarified butter.
2.5.1.33. Having turned toward the *dhruvā* ladle and having anointed the *prastara* bundle, he stands up.
2.5.1.34. Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Sacrifice to Agni."
2.5.1.35. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers [the oblation] on the northern half [of the fire].
2.5.1.36. Saying, "Recite for Soma," he takes four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
2.5.1.37. Having anointed the *dhruvā* ladle and having anointed the *prastara* bundle, he rises.
2.5.1.38. Having stepped across and caused the announcement to be made, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for Soma.
2.5.1.39. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the oblation in the southern half [of the fire].
2.5.1.40. Having spread an underlayer of ghee, touched water, and while taking the portion, he says, "Recite the invitatory prayer for Agni."
2.5.1.41. He cuts portions from both the back and the front of the *aṣṭākapāla* cake, pours clarified butter over them, and anoints them back [with the butter].
2.5.1.42. Having wiped the *dhruvā* ladle and having smeared the *prastara* bundle, he rises up.
2.5.1.43. Having stepped across, he says, "O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! and "Sacrifice to Agni!"
2.5.1.44. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the middle.
2.5.1.45. Having spread [the underlayer] and touched water, while taking the portion, he says: "Recite for Śoma! 2.5.1.46.
At the full moon sacrifice, [he says] in a whisper, "For Viṣṇu"; at the new moon sacrifice, [he says the same].
2.5.1.47. He cuts portions from both the rear and the front of the *caru*, pours clarified butter over them, and anoints the base of the ladle.
2.5.1.48. Having wiped the *dhruvā* spoon and having smeared the *prastara* bundle, he rises up.
2.5.1.49. Having stepped across and caused the announcement to be made, he says: "Sacrifice to so-and-so."
2.5.1.50. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers [the oblation] in the eastern half [of the fire].

2.5.1.51. Having spread a base of clarified butter and touched water, while taking the portion, he says: "Recite for Agni and Soma," at the full moon sacrifice; "for Indra and Agni," at the new moon sacrifice. 2.5.1.52.

For one who has not yet performed a sacrifice, [he takes the portion] saying "for Indra"; for one who has already performed a sacrifice, he takes portions from both the rear and the front of the cake on eleven potsherds.
2.5.1.53. He takes a portion from both the rear and the front of the curd with the dipping-spoon (sruva).

2.5.1.54. He takes a portion from both the rear and the front of the boiled milk with the dipping-spoon. 2.5.1.55. He fills [the vessel] with curd, pours [clarified butter] over it, and anoints [the ladle] in reverse.
2.5.1.56. Having turned toward the *dhruvā* and having anointed the *prastara*, he rises; having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Sacrifice to Indra.
2.5.1.57. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering in the rear half [of the fire].
2.5.1.58. While spreading [ghee] and cutting [the portion], he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt."
2.5.1.59. He makes a single cutting from the northern half of the cake on eight potsherds.
2.5.1.60. He makes a single cutting from the northern half of the porridge with the stirring-spoon.
2.5.1.61. Having made those cuttings, he hands the two spoons down to the Agnīdhra priest.
2.5.1.62. He makes an offering from the northern half of the cake on eleven potsherds once.
2.5.1.63. He makes an offering from the northern half of the curd with the dipping-spoon once.
2.5.1.64. He makes an offering from the northern half of the boiled milk with the dipping-spoon once.
2.5.1.65. He pours [the butter] over the cooked oblation, sprinkles it twice, and does not anoint it back.
2.5.1.66. Having anointed the *dhruvā* [ladle] and having smeared the *prastara* [grass-bundle], he rises up.
2.5.1.67. Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Sacrifice to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt."
2.5.1.68. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering on the northern half, passing over the previous offerings.
2.5.1.69. He throws the stirring-spoon (*mekṣaṇa*) into the fires. 2.5.1.70. He makes an additional libation over that with the residue of the offering.

2.5.1.71. Having stepped across and placed the two *sruva*-ladles in their respective places, he cuts the portion for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt from the cake on eight potsherds; from that same spot, he cuts a portion the size of a barleycorn for the *prāśitra*. 2.5.1.72. Having brought it forward between the *sruva*-ladle and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), and having set it down to the south of the altar, he pours clarified butter over it.
2.5.1.73. Having touched water, performed the ritual purification (*mārjana*), washed [the ladle], and rinsed the handle of the *sruva*-ladle, he spreads an under-layer of butter in the *iḍā*-vessel.
He cuts off a piece of the *puroḍāśa* cake from the southern half of the eight-pot-sherd offering. 2.6.1.2. He places that into the cup.

2.6.1.3. Having divided the portions, he cuts off a four-finger-breadth share for the sacrificer from the eastern half of the cake on eight potsherds. 2.6.1.4. Having placed the dividing marks and having anointed [the portions] with clarified butter, he pushes the sacrificer’s share forward in front of the *dhruvā* ladle; then, having cut a portion from the southern half of the porridge and having divided the portions, he cuts off a second portion. 2.6.1.5.
Having cut a portion from the southern half of the cake on eleven potsherds and having divided the portions, he likewise cuts off a second portion.
2.6.1.6. Having taken a portion from the southern half of the curd with the *sruva* ladle and having stirred the portions together, he takes a second portion.
2.6.1.7. Having taken a portion from the southern half of the boiled milk (*śṛta*) with the *sruva* ladle and having stirred the portions together, he takes a second portion.
2.6.1.8. He fills [the vessel] either with curd or with boiled milk.

2.6.1.9. Or, having sprinkled clarified butter over both [the *iḍā* portions], he places the *iḍā* for the *hotṛ*. 2.6.1.10. Without releasing [the *iḍā*] from the front of the *hotṛ*, he steps across. 2.6.1.11. Having smeared a finger of the *hotṛ* with clarified butter, he spreads it out upon the *hotṛ*'s hand.
2.6.1.12. He cuts [the portion] twice and pours clarified butter over it once. 2.6.1.13.
When the fourfold cutting has been completed, the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer both touch the *anvārambha* of the *iḍā*.

2.6.1.14. When he recognizes [the signal], "The *iḍā* has been invoked," then the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite: "O thou of fair form and excellent color, come hither! Thou art this well-pervading, wealthy, and beloved [portion]; enjoy it; may I obtain thy invitation" (cf. BŚS 3.18:90.17–19).

2.6.1.15. Having prepared an offering on eight potsherds for Barhiṣad, the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite: "O Bradhna, overflow! Let there be no loss for me as I give; let there be no failure for me as I act. You are the ordainer of the quarters; may the quarters be favorable to me; may the quarters be favorable to me. To you, the guardian of the quarters, to the four immortal guardians of the regions, the overseers of what has come to be—we shall pay worship with this oblation. Make the waters overflow, quicken the plants, protect the two-footed, favor the four-footed, and send rain from heaven! Thus he says.

Having placed the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) in the *pātrī* vessel, he places it for the *āgnīdhra* priest for one who has turned toward the west from the east, having twice spread a base of butter and poured butter over it, while making him recite: “May Agni protect me from ill-sacrificed [rites]” over the first portion, and “May Savitṛ [protect me] from the malevolent” over the second.
2.6.1.17. He gazes at the *prāśitra* portion with the formula: “Whosoever acts as an enemy to me, whether near or far, may I conquer him by this. They then consume it.
2.6.1.18. At this time, the Adhvaryu eats three times from the hand with his breath; they sprinkle themselves for purification. 2.6.1.19. [With the mantra:

"May Bṛhaspati extend this sacrifice of ours; may all the gods rejoice here" (TS 1.6.3.2), he continuously carries a fragment of the *aṣṭākapāla* cake along with water to the north of the Āhavanīya fire for the Brahman priest, using the *veda* grass-bundle.
2.6.1.20. The Brahman eats it and sprinkles himself with water for purification.
2.6.1.21. Having touched the Veda with this very [formula], he returns by the same way he came and hands it over to the Adhvaryu.

2.6.1.22. Having thrown the sacrificer’s portion into the *caru*, he places the oblations one after another in order from west to east, behind himself and to the east of the *utkara* heap, turning toward the north.
2.6.1.23. They bring the *anvāhārya* mess of rice.

2.6.1.24. If it should be cooked elsewhere, he should place it on the Anvāhāryapacana fire. 2.6.1.25. If it should be lacking liquid, he should pour clarified butter over it. 2.6.1.26. Over that [food], he makes the wife recite: “Thou art the portion of Prajāpati; full of vigor, full of milk, protect my out-breath and in-breath; protect my common breath and diffused breath; protect my upward breath and diffused breath; thou art imperishable, for the sake of imperishability, mayest thou not perish for me, in yonder world and in this one. (TS 1.6.3r,s,t + iha ca)
2.6.1.27. Having led him past the Brahman and the sacrificer by the eastern side, he seats him within the altar (antarvedi).

2.6.1.28. Upon him, the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite in this very same manner. 2.6.1.29. He causes him to be carried out toward the north, behind himself and in front of the rubbish-heap (utkara), with the words: "To the Āgnīdhra, to the Brahman, to the Hotṛ, to the Adhvaryus!"

2.6.1.30. With the formula, “May the mind, the light, be pleased” (TS 1.6.3.0), and *svāhā*, he offers a continuous stream with the *sruva* ladle, saying: “May Bṛhaspati join together this sacrifice that has been interrupted; may he extend this sacrifice for us; may all the gods rejoice here, *svāhā*. 2.6.1.31. Having said, “Come, O sacrificer,” while the sacrificer maintains contact [with him], he offers the second oblation for the Hotṛ.
2.6.1.32. Then he says: “O Brahman, we shall set forth; having placed a fuel-stick [on the fire], O Āgnīdhra, cleanse the fire once each time.”
2.6.1.33. Having taken hold of the faggot-bands and the wooden sword (sphyá), he wipes the middle enclosing-stick (paridhí) of the fires once.
2.6.1.34. Once the southern one, once the northern one; having wiped the fire once, he throws away the grass-blades in the path of movement.
2.6.1.35. Taking the two offering-spoons (srúc), the Adhvaryu steps across.
2.6.1.36. He says, "O, cause [the gods] to hear! and then, "Sacrifice to the gods! 2.6.1.37.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) in the middle.
2.6.1.38. Saying, "Sacrifice! Sacrifice!", he performs three after-offerings (*anūyāja*), directed westward.
2.6.1.39. Having offered the final oblation, he mixes the eastward-streaming oblations with the residue.
2.6.1.40. Having stepped across and placed the two offering-spoons in their respective places, [he recites]: "May I [attain] the strength...

2.6.2.1. With the mantra, “By the impulse of strength—with the lifting—I have lifted him up” (TS 1.1.13a), he lifts up both the *prastara* and the *juhū* with his right hand, saying, “And now, by the pressing down, Indra has made my rivals low.
2.6.2.2. With his left hand, he presses down on the *upabhṛt*, saying, “May they separate the lifting and the pressing down” (TS 1.1.13b).
2.6.2.3. He moves the *juhū* forward and pushes the *upabhṛt* backward.

2.6.2.4. Having combined the *prastara* into his left hand, he anoints the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) with the offering-ladle (*sruk*), saying, “I anoint you for the Vasus”; [he anoints] the southern one, saying, “I anoint you for the Rudras”; [and he anoints] the northern one, saying, “I anoint you for the Ādityas. 2.6.2.5. Having broken off a chip from the middle enclosing-stick, he places it into the *juhū* ladle.
2.6.2.6. Holding the middle enclosing-stick with the *sruk*, he causes the announcement to be made; [the Adhvaryu] says, “O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! (*o śrāvaya*).

2.6.2.7. "The divine invokers have been impelled for the auspicious recitation; the human one has been sent forth for the *sūktavāka*. Recite the hymns!"—having thus thrown [the grass-bundle] into the fire, having placed the wood-shavings down, and having brought back the *juhū* ladle, he anoints the *upabhṛt*, the *prastara*, and the spoons. 2.6.2.8. With the words, "Licking that which is anointed," he anoints the tips [of the *prastara*] in the *juhū*; with "May the branches spread out," the middle part; and having brought them near, with "May the waters and the plants swell," the roots in the *dhruvā*. Having anointed them three times each, he throws the *prastara* into the fire with the words, "Thou art the spotted deer of the Maruts."
2.6.2.9. With the words, "O Vaśā, having become spotted, go to heaven" (TS 1.1.13d var), he gazes at the rising smoke, [saying] "From there, send rain upon us.
2.6.2.10. With the words, "Bestow wealth," he removes a blade of grass from the *prastara* bundle with his left hand.
2.6.2.11. He places that [blade] into the *juhū* ladle.
2.6.2.12. When he knows, “This sacrificer, so-and-so, desires this,” then he throws the entire *prastara* [grass-bundle] into the fire.

2.6.2.13. Having pulled out a blade of grass from the *prastara* and having smeared it on the *juhū* ladle, he says to the *āgnīdhra*, “Say this! 2.6.2.14. “Throw it after [the *prastara*] and respond to the call,” says the *āgnīdhra*.
2.6.2.15. The Adhvaryu says, "The Agnīdh has come," and the Agnīdh replies, "He has come.

2.6.2.16. The Adhvaryu says, "Make it heard," and the Agnīdh replies, "Śrauṣaṭ. 2.6.2.17. He offers [the oblation] following [the call], saying: "May there be well-being for the divine Hotṛs; may there be prosperity for the human ones; speak the word of peace!"* *Note: The term *śaṃyo* is understood here as an archaic or variant form of *śaṃyoḥ* (genitive dual of *śam*), meaning "of peace" or "for the sake of peace."*
2.6.2.18. Having touched the inner enclosing-stick with the formula, “Thou art firm,” he touches himself with the formula, “May I become through thee.

2.6.2.19. Having touched water, he touches his vital breaths with the formulas: “Thou art the protector of life, O Agni; protect my life”; “Thou art the protector of sight, O Agni; protect my sight”; “Thou art the protector of hearing, O Agni; protect my hearing” (TS 1.1.13.i). (See also ŚB 1.1.9:29.10.)
2.6.2.20. With the mantra, “The enclosing-stick which you have placed around,” he throws the middle enclosing-stick after [the fire], with the words, “O divine Agni, be mindful of the Paṇis.
2.6.2.21. With the mantra, “The beloved, drinkable portion of Agni,” he throws [the other two] enclosing-sticks on both sides.

2.6.2.22. When he knows [the verse], “May the medicine go upward,” then he lifts up the two offering-spoons together with the words, “You who possess a share in the remnants, rejoice upon the sacrificial grass.”

2.6.2.23. Having poured the residue from the *dhruvā* ladle [into the *ājyasthālī*] with the formula, “Ye are the ghee-dripping ones,” he anoints the *dhruvā* on both sides of the two offering-ladles (*sruc*) with the formula, “O ye two, protect the burden-bearer at the yoke.
2.6.2.24. With the formula, “I set you two down in the seat of Agni whose house is secure” (TS 1.1.13p), he places the *juhū* on the wooden sword (*sphya*).
2.6.2.25. He does not let the *upabhṛt* touch [the *juhū*].
2.6.2.26. With the mantra, "Bestow [us] for the sake of prosperity" (TS 1.1.13q), he takes up the *sruva* and the *juhū* ladles. 2.6.2.27. He hands the *veda* grass-bundle to the *hotṛ*.
2.6.2.28. To the south of the *gārhapatya* fire, both the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer enter; to the north, both the *hotṛ* and the *āgnīdhra*.
2.6.2.29. Having touched water, he places a chip from the kindling wood upon the Gārhapatya fire.
2.6.2.30. Having sat down to the west of the Gārhapatya fire, facing eastward, they perform the *saṃyājana* offerings for the wives.
2.6.2.31. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Soma."
2.6.2.32. While taking the clarified butter, he says four times, "O, cause [the fire] to hear! and then, "Sacrifice to Soma! 2.6.2.33. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers it in the middle.
2.6.2.34. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Tvaṣṭṛ."
2.6.2.35. Taking portions of clarified butter alone, he says four times: “O Śrāvaya,” and “Sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ. 2.6.2.36. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering.
2.6.2.37. He says: “Recite the invitatory verse for Rākā.”

2.6.2.38. Taking portions of clarified butter alone, he says four times, “O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! and “Sacrifice to Rākā! 2.6.2.39. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering.
2.6.2.40. He says, “Recite the invitatory verse for the wives of the gods.”

2.6.2.41. Taking portions of clarified butter itself, he says four times, "O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! and then, "Sacrifice to the wives of the gods. 2.6.2.42. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering.
2.6.2.43. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Gṛhapati."
2.6.2.44. Taking portions of clarified butter alone, he says four times, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard," and then, "Sacrifice to Agni Gṛhapati.
2.6.2.45. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering on the northern half of the fire, passing over the previous offerings.
2.6.2.46. Having placed the *sruk* ladle on the *vedī*, and having smeared the thumb of the Hotṛ with clarified butter, he places the four-fold portion of the *iḍā* into the hand of the Hotṛ.
2.6.2.47. The Adhvaryu, the sacrificer, and the wife take hold [of the Agnīdh] from behind.
2.6.2.48. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the portions] twice for the Agnīdh, who has turned toward the east from the north. 2.6.2.49. They consume [the portions].
2.6.2.50. They sprinkle themselves with water, saying: "May Bṛhaspati extend this sacrifice for us; may all the gods rejoice here! (TS 1.6.3.3o2 [= 1.5.3.2g2]; cf. BŚS 3.18:90.20).

2.6.2.51. [The Adhvaryu] offers the *patnīhoma* with the *sruva*-ladle continuously until [the verse for] the wife: while the wife holds on to him, he offers with the formula: “May the wife go together with her husband to their good deeds! May they become the two yoke-horses of the sacrifice; as they move forward, may they abandon the adversary. May you both seize the highest light in heaven, svāhā! (Cf. MS 1.4.3a:51.4; 1.4.8:56.10; KS 5.4a:32.4; TB 3.7.5.11a; ĀpŚS 3.9.10a; MŚS 1.3.5.5).
2.6.2.52. Having cut off a blade of grass from the *veda* and having smeared it with clarified butter from both the *juhū* and the *ājyasthālī*, he says to the *āgnīdhra*, "Say this. 2.6.2.53.
"Throw it into the fire and respond," says the *adhvaryu*.
2.6.2.54. "The *āgnīdhra* has come," says the *adhvaryu*; "He has come," says the *āgnīdhra*.

2.6.2.55. The Adhvaryu says, “Make [them] hear,” and the Āgnīdhra says, “Śrauṣaṭ. 2.6.2.56. He offers the oblation, saying, “May there be prosperity for the divine Hotṛs; may there be well-being for the human ones; proclaim auspiciousness and peace! 2.6.2.57.
When he knows [the verse], “May the medicine go upward,” then he takes up both the dipping-spoon (sruva) and the offering-ladle (sruk) together.
2.6.2.58. He takes four portions [of clarified butter] and pours in the husks of the grain. 2.6.2.59. He offers that as a libation. 2.6.2.60.

Having approached with the Veda-bundle, he performs the husk-libation on the Anvāhāryapacana fire with the formula: "O Agni of unimpaired life-force, O thou of cool body, protect our womb! Svāhā! (TS 1.1.13).
2.6.2.61. He takes up both the *sruva* and the *juhū* ladles. 2.6.2.62. He hands the *veda* grass-bundle to the *hotṛ*.
2.6.2.63. Having gone forward to the east, he causes the *dhruvā* vessel to swell [with clarified butter], [reciting]: "May it swell..."
“May the firm ones cause [the sacrificer] to swell with clarified butter; may the earth [cause him to swell] at every sacrifice in this sacrifice. 2.6.3.2.

Having gathered the grass of the *veda* with the *barhis*, he offers with the ladle [reciting]: “O gods who know the way” (*TS* 1.1.13), [and] “Having found the way, [may there be] *svāhā* to speech in the sacrifice.”

2.6.3.3. Having smeared the *barhis* grass on the *dhruvā* ladle with the formula, "May the *barhis* be anointed with the oblation, with clarified butter," he throws it after [the offering] with the formula, "Anointed together with the Ādityas, with the Vasus, with the Maruts, with Indra, with all the gods; may it go to the celestial sky, Svāhā! 2.6.3.4. With the formula, "Svāhā! Place [it] in the wind," he makes an additional offering from the residue above.

2.6.3.5. Having set down the *sruk* ladle to the east of the *āhavanīya* fire and having brought forward half of the *praṇītā* water, he pours it into the joined palms of the sacrificer within the altar.

2.6.3.6. Having filled [the vessel], he makes [the sacrificer] recite over the *pūrṇapātra*: “Thou art real; mayest thou be real for me! Thou art all; thou art imperishable; mayest thou not perish for me! (cf. TS 1.6.5c). 2.6.3.7.
With the words, “May the gods and the officiating priests purify [us] in the eastern direction” (TS 1.6.5d), he pours [water] into the joined palms of the sacrificer.

2.6.3.8. Having set down the vessel with the words, “May the months, the ancestors, and the lord of sacrifice purify themselves in the southern direction” (TS 1.6.5d), he rises and, following along the southern edge of the altar, strides the Viṣṇu-strides with the formulas: “This is the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the adversary... [repeated] ...in the directions; he whom we hate is excluded” (TS 1.6.5e–h). 2.6.3.9. With the words, “We have gone to the light, to the world of light” (TS 1.6.6a), he strides forward toward the east.

2.6.3.10. He worships the sun with the formula: "May I not be cut off from your sight. [He continues: "Whatever heat is yours, for that [heat] of yours, I exclude this evil rival from these quarters, from this earth, and from this food; being excluded, may I become united with light. (TS 1.6.6b1+d4+e) 2.6.3.11. "I turn following the turning of Indra," he says, and turns toward the right.
2.6.3.12. At that very moment he turns back with the formula: "May I be at peace with my offspring and with the increase of wealth. (TS 1.6.6g)

2.6.3.13. With the words, “Kindled, O Agni, shine for me,” he either kindles [the fire] or places a fuel-stick upon it, saying, “May I shine, well-kindled by thee, O Agni; svāhā! (TS 1.6.6i + svāhā). 2.6.3.14.
With the words, “May the sacrifice be rich in wealth; may I become more wealthy,” (TS 1.6.6k) he worships [the fire]. 2.6.3.15.

With the two verses addressed to Agni-Pavamāna, beginning with “O Agni, thou purifiest the lives,” (TS 1.6.6l–m), he approaches the Gārhapatya fire, [concluding] with the words, “Bring hither to me strength, food, and wealth.”

2.6.3.16. He worships with the formula, “O Agni, lord of the house! [as in TS 1.6.6n]: “May I be a good lord of the house through you as my lord of the house; may you be a good lord of the house through me as your lord of the house. 2.6.3.17. He invokes blessings: “A hundred winters—this blessing I invoke for myself, for so-and-so, full of light. First he mentions his own name, then “for so-and-so, for so-and-so,” in successive order for his sons, ending with “the lineage.
2.6.3.18. With the formula, “He who yokes you, let him release you” (TS 1.6.6o), he gazes at the mortar and pestle from a distance.

2.6.3.19. With the words, “The potsherds which [were used] in the cauldron,” they collect the potsherds; with the words, “Let them be released” (TS 1.1.7k). 2.6.3.20. With the words, “The sacrifice has come into being; it has manifested itself” (TS 1.6.6q), he goes eastward by taking hold of the sacrifice again: “It was born; it grew; it [is the source] of the gods’ riches. 2.6.3.21. Having stepped forward to the east, he mutters: “O Agni, the sacrifice rich in cattle, rich in sheep, rich in horses” (TS 1.6.6r); “A friend of the Ṛgveda, a leader in the assembly” (TS 1.6.6r).

2.6.3.22. Standing to the south, he releases the vow. 2.6.3.23. With the formula, “The plants are rich in milk,” he sips water through the strainer with the formula, “Rich in milk, O herb, unite [me]” (TS 1.5.10g).

2.6.3.24. Having performed the purification with the formula, “O Agni, lord of the vow,” he places a fuel-stick on the fire with the formula, “I have observed the vow; I was able to do it; it has been accomplished for me, svāhā! (TS 1.5.10h var.).
2.6.3.25. Having come back, he unties the wife who is seated to the west of the *gārhapatya* fire with the mantra: "I loosen this [bond] from my body" (*TS* 1.1.10g-h). 2.6.3.26.
With the mantra, "The plants are rich in milk," he sips water through the strainer with the mantra, "Rich in milk... unite" (*TS* 1.5.10g). 2.6.3.27.

Having purified himself with the mantra, "O Agni, lord of vows" (*TS* 1.5.10h var), he places a fuel-stick on the fire with the mantra: "We have performed the vow; we were able to do it; may it be successful for me, *svāhā*" (*TS* 1.5.10h).

2.6.3.28. The wife returns; having sat down to the south, she eats the sacrificer’s portion with the formula: “The radiance of Prajāpati, together with the sacrificer” (TS 1.6.5.b). 2.6.3.29. The New and Full Moon sacrifices are completed. The New and Full Moon sacrifices are completed.
